title: Wukong Framework for Not Safe For Work Detection in Text-to-Image Systems

problem.claim: Text-to-image systems can generate NSFW content that violates community guidelines, creating a need for efficient and accurate detection.

gap.claim: Text-based safeguards overlook model-specific variations and are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, while image-based safeguards are computationally costly and introduce latency.

contributions.claim: Wukong is a transformer-based NSFW detection framework that uses intermediate outputs from early denoising steps and reuses pretrained U-Net cross-attention parameters.
Wukong operates within the diffusion process to enable detection before full image generation completes.
The authors introduce a dataset containing prompts, seeds, and image-specific NSFW labels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating Wukong on the introduced dataset and two public benchmarks.
The authors report that Wukong significantly outperforms text-based safeguards, achieves comparable accuracy to image filters, and offers greater efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text-to-image generation enables diverse image synthesis but can produce NSFW content.
Efficient and accurate external safeguarding is needed, while existing text and image filters have important limitations.
Early denoising steps define semantic layout, and U-Net cross-attention aligns text with image regions.
Wukong uses early denoising outputs and pretrained cross-attention parameters for in-process detection.
The authors introduce a labeled dataset and report results across it and two public benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Early denoising steps define image semantics, and cross-attention aligns text with image regions.

interpretation.claim: Intermediate representations may support earlier safety decisions than fully rendered outputs.

application.claim: For iterative generative systems, investigate safety checks over intermediate states to reduce latency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether intermediate-state detection preserves safety coverage across all generation behaviors.

source_observation.claim: Text filters miss model-specific variations, while image filters add computational cost and latency.

interpretation.claim: Safety mechanisms can trade off input-level coverage, output fidelity, and runtime efficiency.

application.claim: Combine model-internal signals with benchmarked safeguards when designing generation-time moderation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how Wukong handles adversarial prompts or model architectures beyond the described diffusion setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset size, label construction details, or benchmark composition.
The abstract does not provide quantitative accuracy, efficiency, latency, or computational-cost measurements.
The abstract does not specify the evaluation protocol, baselines, or statistical uncertainty.
